expected.bio: Rock Hudson was an American actor. One of the most popular film stars of his time, he had a screen career spanning more than three decades, and was a prominent figure in the Golden Age of Hollywood.

changes.description: Hollywood actor whose documented life as a gay man and death from AIDS-related complications in 1985 connect his story to gay history and public awareness of AIDS.

expected.bio: Anna-Lou Leibovitz is an American portrait photographer best known for her portraits, particularly of celebrities, which often feature subjects in intimate settings and poses. Leibovitz's Polaroid photo of John Lennon and Yoko Ono, taken five hours before Lennon's murder, is considered one of Rolling Stone magazine's most famous cover photographs. The Library of Congress declared her a Living Legend, and she is the first woman to have a feature exhibition at Washington's National Portrait Gallery.

changes.lgbti_details: A Guardian interview describes Leibovitz and writer Susan Sontag as a couple and discusses photographs collected in A Photographer’s Life. The book’s record of the two women’s shared life documents a connection through the representation of a same-sex relationship.

expected.bio: Waheed Alli, Baron Alli is a British media entrepreneur and politician. He has held executive positions at several television production companies including the Endemol Shine Group, Carlton Television Productions, Planet 24, and Chorion. Alli served as the Chief Executive of Silvergate Media until 2022, Chairman of Koovs Plc and a director at Olga Productions. He is a member of the House of Lords in the United Kingdom, sitting as a life peer for the Labour Party, and is described as one of only a few openly gay Muslim politicians in the world.

expected.bio: Lee Grinner Pace is an American actor. He starred as Thranduil the Elvenking in The Hobbit trilogy and as Joe MacMillan in the period drama television series Halt and Catch Fire. He has also appeared in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ronan the Accuser, a role he first played in Guardians of the Galaxy and reprised in Captain Marvel. Pace earned a 2008 Emmy nomination for his portrayal of Ned in the comedy-drama Pushing Daisies. Since 2021, he has starred as the galactic emperor Brother Day in the Foundation television series, based on the stories of Isaac Asimov.

changes.lgbti_details: In an Attitude interview, Jessup reflects on his public coming-out in June 2019 and describes the relief it brought. He discusses wanting to live openly after falling in love, providing a direct public account of his connection.

expected.bio: Enrique Martín Morales, known professionally as Ricky Martin, is a Puerto Rican singer, songwriter and actor. He is known for his musical versatility, with his discography incorporating a wide variety of many elements, such as Latin pop, dance, reggaeton, salsa, and other genres. Born in San Juan, Martin began appearing in television commercials at age nine and began his musical career at twelve, as a member of Puerto Rican boy band Menudo. He began his solo career in 1991 while in Sony Music Mexico, gaining recognition in Latin America with the release of his first two studio albums, Ricky Martin (1991) and Me Amaras (1993), both of which were focused on ballads.

expected.description: American artist, film director, and producer (1928–1987)
expected.bio: Andy Warhol was an American visual artist, film director and producer. A leading figure in the pop art movement, Warhol is considered one of the most important American artists of the second half of the 20th century. His works explore the relationship between artistic expression, advertising, and celebrity culture that flourished by the 1960s, and span a variety of media, including painting, sculpture, photography, and filmmaking. Some of his best-known works include the silkscreen paintings Campbell's Soup Cans (1962) and Marilyn Diptych (1962), the experimental film Chelsea Girls (1966), the multimedia events known as the Exploding Plastic Inevitable (1966–67), and the erotic film Blue Movie (1969) that started the "Golden Age of Porn".

changes.description: Artist whose museum documents his queer identity and its expression in art, from drawings of men in the 1950s to self-portraits in drag in the 1980s.
changes.bio: Andy Warhol was an artist whose work is preserved and interpreted by the Andy Warhol Museum. Its LGBTQ programme explores how sexuality shaped his art and relationships, including drawings from the 1950s and self-portraits from the 1980s.
changes.lgbti_details: The Andy Warhol Museum explicitly connects Warhol's queer identity with his life and art. It points to his drawings of men, self-portraits in drag and romantic relationships, situating his work within the history of gay visibility.

expected.description: American lawyer and transgender rights activist
expected.bio: Chase Strangio is an American lawyer and transgender rights activist. He is the deputy director for transgender justice and staff attorney with the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU). He is the first known transgender person to make oral arguments before the Supreme Court of the United States.

changes.description: ACLU lawyer whose litigation and advocacy defend LGBTQ people and people living with HIV, including Supreme Court arguments about transgender young people's healthcare.
changes.bio: Chase Strangio is a lawyer with the ACLU's LGBTQ and HIV rights project. His work has included the Sylvia Rivera Law Project, co-founding the Lorena Borjas Community Fund and representing plaintiffs in major civil-rights cases.
changes.lgbti_details: The ACLU documents Strangio's work in litigation and advocacy for LGBTQ people and people living with HIV. His cases include challenges to discrimination against trans people and oral arguments in U.S. v. Skrmetti in December 2024.

de.lgbti_details: Die ACLU dokumentiert Strangios Gerichtsverfahren und politischen Einsatz für LGBTQ-Menschen und Menschen mit HIV. Dazu gehören Verfahren gegen die Diskriminierung von trans Menschen und sein Vortrag im Fall U.S. v. Skrmetti im Dezember 2024.
de.bio: Chase Strangio ist Anwalt beim LGBTQ- und HIV-Rechteprojekt der ACLU. Er arbeitete beim Sylvia Rivera Law Project, gründete den Lorena Borjas Community Fund mit und vertrat Klägerinnen und Kläger in bedeutenden Bürgerrechtsverfahren.

She also pursues a solo career, releasing ten albums under her own name, and founded the independent label Daemon Records in 1989. Ray is known for her alto and tenor range, and plays both electric and acoustic guitar, as well as mandolin and harmonica.

expected.description: Swiss journalist, activist, and politician known for her pro-LGBTQ advocacy and service on the National Council since 2023.
expected.bio:
Anna Rosenwasser (born 1 May 1990 in Schaffhausen) is a Swiss journalist, editorialist, writer, and politician. She is affiliated with the Social Democratic Party and has served on the National Council (Switzerland) since 2023.

Rosenwasser gained public recognition in Switzerland for her commitment to LGBT rights, with a particular focus on same-sex marriage. She is an outspoken critic of homophobia and discrimination against sexual minorities.

Her professional and political activities are closely linked to her advocacy for LGBTQ rights, establishing her as a prominent pro-LGBTQ activist in Switzerland.

changes.bio: Anna Rosenwasser is a Swiss author and politician whose work focuses on feminism and LGBTQ issues. Her books include Rosa Buch and Herz, and her biography describes journalism, public talks and workshops on queer identities.
changes.lgbti_details: Rosenwasser's official biography records her work as director of the Swiss Lesbian Organisation from 2017 to 2021, earlier involvement in Milchjugend and co-founding AnderSH. She explicitly describes her commitment to the queer community.

expected.description: German journalist; Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2016

expected.description: incumbent Mayor of Zurich; Swiss politician, 1960–
expected.bio: Corine Mauch is an American-born Swiss politician who currently serves as Mayor of Zurich since 2009. She previously served on the city council of Zürich between 1999 and 2008 for the Social Democratic Party of Switzerland. Mauch is the first female and first openly lesbian person to be elected mayor of the city.

de.bio: Corine Mauch ist eine Schweizer SP-Politikerin und wurde 2009 zur Zürcher Stadtpräsidentin gewählt. Zeitgenössische Berichte beschrieben ihr Interesse an Umweltfragen und Musik sowie die Bedeutung ihrer Wahl für Frauen und lesbische Sichtbarkeit.

expected.bio: Danica Anthony Roem is an American journalist and politician who has served in the Virginia Senate since 2024. A Democrat, she represents the 30th district covering part of Prince William County including the cities of Manassas and Manassas Park. She previously served in the Virginia House of Delegates representing the 13th district from 2018-2024.

changes.description: Virginia politician whose LGBTQ advocacy includes legislation against discrimination in health insurance and support for inclusive schools, documented by HRC.
changes.bio: Danica Roem is a Virginia politician who became the first openly transgender person elected to the state's General Assembly. HRC's account of her legislative work describes efforts on health-insurance equality and inclusive learning environments.
changes.lgbti_details: HRC documents Roem's advocacy for LGBTQ rights, including a bill passed in 2020 against health-insurance discrimination affecting transgender Virginians. It also records her support for protections against discrimination in schools.

de.lgbti_details: HRC dokumentiert Roems Einsatz für LGBTQ-Rechte, darunter ein 2020 verabschiedetes Gesetz gegen die Benachteiligung von trans Menschen durch Krankenversicherungen in Virginia. Die Organisation nennt auch ihren Einsatz gegen Diskriminierung an Schulen.
de.bio: Danica Roem wurde als erste offen trans Person in Virginias General Assembly gewählt. HRC beschreibt ihre parlamentarische Arbeit für Gleichberechtigung bei Krankenversicherungen und ein inklusives Lernumfeld.

expected.description: Ernst Ostertag is a Swiss LGBTQ rights activist from Winterthur, dedicated to promoting equality and inclusivity for the LGBTQ+ community. As an advocate, Ostertag has worked tirelessly to advance the rights and visibility of LGBTQ+ individuals in Switzerland and beyond. Through his activism, Ostertag has made a significant impact on the LGBTQ+ community, contributing to a more just and accepting society.

changes.description: Swiss gay-rights campaigner whose activism with Röbi Rapp began in the 1950s and whose story was told in the 2014 film The Circle.
changes.bio: Ernst Ostertag is a Swiss gay-rights campaigner whose long relationship with Röbi Rapp became part of the film The Circle in 2014. In 2003 they were the first couple to register a same-sex partnership in canton Zurich.
changes.lgbti_details: A Keystone-SDA report published by SWI swissinfo.ch records Ostertag and Röbi Rapp's gay-rights activism from the 1950s. It also documents their 2003 partnership registration in canton Zurich, connecting their lives to Swiss equality history.

de.lgbti_details: Ein Keystone-SDA-Bericht bei SWI swissinfo.ch dokumentiert Ostertags und Röbi Rapps Einsatz für die Rechte homosexueller Menschen seit den 1950ern. Er nennt auch ihre eingetragene Partnerschaft 2003 im Kanton Zürich und verbindet ihr Leben mit Schweizer Gleichberechtigungsgeschichte.

expected.bio: George Takei, born Hosato Takei , is an American actor, author and activist known for his role as Hikaru Sulu, helmsman of the USS Enterprise in the Star Trek franchise.

expected.bio: Colin Michael Maurice Cashman, Baron Cashman, is a British actor, dancer, politician, and LGBT rights activist. A member of the Labour Party, he served as a Member of the European Parliament for the West Midlands from 1999 to 2014. He has been a member of the House of Lords since 2014. He is a patron of Humanists UK.

changes.description: Actor, writer and politician whose parliamentary record documents his role as co-founder and founding chair of Stonewall, the LGBTQ equality organization.
changes.bio: Michael Cashman has worked as an actor, writer and politician. His parliamentary record includes service as a European Parliament member from 1999 to 2014 and co-founding Stonewall in 1989.
changes.lgbti_details: Cashman's official parliamentary experience record lists him as Stonewall co-founder and founding chair from 1989 to 1994. This supplies a concrete, documented connection through the establishment and leadership of an LGBTQ rights organization.

expected.bio: Hayley Kiyoko Alcroft is an American singer-songwriter, actress, and author. As a child model and actress, she appeared in a variety of films, including Lemonade Mouth (2011), Jem and the Holograms (2015), Insidious: Chapter 3 (2015), and XOXO (2016). Alongside her film roles, she also had a recurring role in the TV series' Wizards of Waverly Place (2010) and The Fosters (2014); and lead roles on CSI: Cyber (2015–2016) and Five Points (2018–2019).

changes.description: Singer and filmmaker whose support for LGBTQ young people, transgender visibility and fundraising for The Trevor Project are documented in its 2019 award announcement.
changes.bio: Hayley Kiyoko is a singer and music-video director. In a 2019 award announcement she described sharing experiences of love and identity through her work, while The Trevor Project recognised her support for LGBTQ young people.
changes.lgbti_details: Variety's report on The Trevor Project's 2019 Youth Innovator Award documents Kiyoko's work for LGBTQ young people. It describes fundraising, support for homeless LGBTQ youth and a music video used to raise awareness of violence against trans women.

de.description: Sängerin und Filmemacherin, deren Unterstützung junger LGBTQ-Menschen, trans Sichtbarkeit und Spendenarbeit für The Trevor Project eine Auszeichnungsankündigung 2019 dokumentiert.
de.lgbti_details: Variety berichtet zum Youth Innovator Award von The Trevor Project 2019 über Kiyokos Einsatz für junge LGBTQ-Menschen. Genannt werden Spendenarbeit, Unterstützung wohnungsloser LGBTQ-Jugendlicher und ein Musikvideo gegen Gewalt gegenüber trans Frauen.
de.bio: Hayley Kiyoko ist Sängerin und Musikvideoregisseurin. In einer Auszeichnungsankündigung 2019 beschrieb sie, wie ihre Arbeit Erfahrungen mit Liebe und Identität teilt. The Trevor Project würdigte ihre Unterstützung junger LGBTQ-Menschen.
